title: Unfair Golf
blurb: An 8-hole browser golf game where every hole breaks a different rule of physics instead of just adding a hazard: gusting wind, a near-frictionless green, an inverse-square gravity well, teleporter pads, a drifting cup, and mirrored controls. Every wall bounce also carries randomized restitution, so no rebound is ever quite predictable.

title: Pixel Plumber
blurb: A tiny Super-Mario-like platformer in plain HTML5 Canvas, with a low-gravity zone and a frictionless ice zone that swap out the physics constants live, plus a toggleable readout of g, friction and the predicted jump height wherever you're standing. The jump-arc physics (h = v0^2/2g) checked against the live game to within ~5%.

title: Glowmeter
blurb: A phone web app that sets an ESP32-S3's onboard LED (colour + brightness) and streams a live measurement back as a strip chart at 20 Hz, over one WebSocket, no server in between. Runs unmodified class-board-2026 firmware; only the phone app is new, and it's flashed onto the board's own filesystem so it's served locally, avoiding any HTTPS/WebSocket mixed-content issue.

title: Cart-pole — the reference example
blurb: The instructor's reference for a Project-1-style build: a cart-pole you can push and balance, drawn on a canvas in plain JavaScript. Use it to see the shape of a finished entry; yours replaces it on the wall.
